units.title: Welcome to Discover Your Divine Design
units.lessonMainIdea: You are On Purpose and you are For Purpose.

media.label: Welcome to your Discover Your Divine Design journey

lessonBody.text: We are pleased to welcome to the Discover Your Divine Design Journey! This course is the heart of the DYDD ecosystem and the best place to start. Our prayer for your journey is that you are able to fully grasp that you are On Purpose and that you are For Purpose.
For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.

You are extremely valuable. In Ephesians 2:10, God calls you His handiwork. Think of this as a materpiece, a work of art, or His poetry. You are no accident, you are On Purpose. The second half of the verse says that God has planned good works for us to do. We are not intended to sit on the sidelines. Our relational journey with Jesus is intended to be action oriented. You are For Purpose. Jesus wants to be part of the Good Work Force, carrying out His mission through love and service.

This is a journey. If you dig, you will find your divine design. This is a process and not a destination. The intent is to help you discover new perspective and utilize your highly valuable and unique contribution to enage.

transcript.text: Welcome to Discover Your Divine Design. Do not treat this like a race to finish content. units.title: Course Outline & Objectives
units.lessonMainIdea: God created you on purpose—with a design worth discovering.

media.label: The six areas of Discover Your Divine Design

lessonBody.text: God created you on purpose—with a design worth discovering. This journey will help you recognize the threads He has woven into your life and consider how to put them into practice.
Together, we’ll explore six areas:

items: Identity — How you are uniquely designed.
Expertise — The abilities and experience you have developed.
Story — The experiences that have shaped you.
Desire — The interests and burdens that move your heart.
Gifts — How God has equipped you to serve others.
Niche — Where these discoveries come together in meaningful contribution.

lessonBody.text: By the end, you’ll have a clearer understanding of your design, words to express it, and practical next steps for living it out.
You don’t need to have your purpose figured out before you begin. That’s what this journey is for.

units.title: How This Journey Works
units.lessonMainIdea: Move through the lessons in order, at a pace that gives you room to reflect.

media.label: A traveler exploring the map

lessonBody.text: Move through the lessons in order, at a pace that gives you room to reflect. Read or watch the teaching, consider the questions, and write honestly about what you’re discovering. This isn’t about finding impressive answers. It’s about paying attention to what God is revealing through your design and your life.
When it’s time to take an assessment or complete a related learning experience, the lesson will guide you. There’s no need to jump ahead or figure it all out now.

Your changed written reflections save when you complete or leave a lesson and are gathered in your Field Kit—your personal place to revisit what you’re discovering. We’ll introduce the reflection tools when you reach them.
If you’re walking through this with a group, follow your facilitator’s schedule and come ready to share what you feel comfortable discussing.
Take your time. You’re not just finishing a course—you’re learning to recognize and live out your God-given design.

title: What is DYDD?
summary: Saved by grace, designed on purpose, and invited to walk in the good works God prepared for us.

units.title: What is DYDD?
units.lessonMainIdea: Recognize how God has uniquely shaped you and where your life can contribute to His work.

media.label: Discover Your Divine Design

lessonBody.text: Discover Your Divine Design exists to help believers recognize how God has uniquely shaped them and where their lives can contribute to His work. When a church walks through this journey together, participants begin to see themselves and one another through a new lens. Rather than simply asking where help is needed, people begin to understand how their God given design can serve the body of Christ and the world around them.

The goal of DYDD is not simply to complete a study or identify a label. The goal is to help believers recognize how God has designed them and to begin living more intentionally within the good works He has prepared for them. They become part of the Good Work force! As participants move forward in faith, the church often sees people serving with renewed joy, deeper purpose, and a clearer understanding of their role within the body of Christ.

units.title: Grace
units.lessonMainIdea: We are saved by grace, designed on purpose, and invited to walk in the good works God prepared for us.

media.label: Saved by grace, designed on purpose

lessonBody.text: Saved by Grace – Designed on Purpose - Walking in the Good Works Prepared for Us

For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast. For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.

Discover Your Divine Design begins with the truth of this passage. Ephesians 2:8–10 reveals the full story of the Christian life. It shows how salvation begins, how God forms His people, and how He intends them to live. These verses remind us that our relationship with God begins with grace, continues through His intentional design, and unfolds through the good works He prepared for us long before we ever recognized them.
DYDD is built around this movement. We are saved by grace, designed on purpose, and invited to walk in the good works God prepared for us.
Saved by Grace

The foundation of everything begins with grace. Salvation is not something we achieve through effort, talent, or accomplishment. It is a gift from God. We are brought into relationship with Him through faith, not through our own performance or ability.

This truth protects the entire journey of discovering our design. Purpose is not about earning God's approval or proving our value. Instead, it grows from the security of knowing we already belong to Him. When people understand they are saved by grace, they are free to explore how God created them without pressure, comparison, or striving.
Designed on Purpose
Ephesians continues by reminding us that we are God's handiwork. The word used in this passage points to something carefully crafted, something formed with intention and care.

Every believer has been uniquely shaped by God. Our story, identity, experiences, abilities, desires, and spiritual gifts all reflect aspects of how He formed us. Discover Your Divine Design helps people recognize this intentional design. Rather than seeing their life as random or disconnected, participants begin to see how God has been shaping them for meaningful contribution.
Walking in Good Works Prepared for Us
The passage ends with a powerful reminder. God not only saves and shapes us, He prepares a path for us to walk.

Good works are not something we invent for ourselves. Scripture tells us that God prepared them in advance. Our role is to recognize where He is leading and step into those opportunities with faith and obedience.

This is the heart of the DYDD journey. As people understand their design, they begin to see where their life can serve others, strengthen the church, and reflect the work God is already doing around them. Discovering our design is not the final goal. The goal is to live faithfully in the good works God has prepared for us.

lessonBody.text: The Mission & Vision Behind DYDD
Mission: On Purpose
Discover Your Divine Design exists to help people rediscover who they are in Christ. Scripture tells us that we are God’s workmanship, His masterpiece, created intentionally and uniquely by Him.

Through biblical teaching, reflection, and practical tools, DYDD helps people gain clarity about their identity, story, gifts, and design so they can live with confidence in who God created them to be.
For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus…
Vision: For Purpose
We envision a Church where believers understand their design and joyfully participate in the work God has prepared for them.
When people discover their identity and embrace their unique contribution, they find belonging, meaningful service, and a deeper sense of calling within the Body of Christ.
…to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
Discover Your Divine Design helps believers understand how God uniquely created them so they can live and serve with clarity and purpose.

units.title: D.E.S.I.G.N
units.lessonMainIdea: Explore six key areas that together reveal how God has uniquely shaped you.

media.label: The elements of your divine design

lessonBody.text: Design is used as an acronym to represent the process taken for Discovery. It is not completed in the order of the acronym, on purpose. The process was carefully developed to help participants build from section to section, constantly gaining ground in their understanding.

The DYDD journey helps participants explore six key areas of their life that together reveal how God has uniquely shaped them. Each element offers a different perspective on how God forms a person through identity, experiences, passions, and spiritual empowerment. As participants reflect on these areas, they often begin to see patterns that reveal how their design may connect with the good works God has prepared for them.
Identity

It all begins with knowing whose you are. Before we can understand what we are called to do, we must first understand who we are in Christ. Identity provides the foundation for the entire journey because our sense of purpose flows from our relationship with God and the truth of what He says about us.
Participants often find themselves reflecting on questions such as:

items: Have I been carrying labels that do not reflect God’s truth about me?
What does Scripture reveal about my identity in Christ?
How might seeing myself through God’s perspective change the way I live and serve?

lessonBody.text: Expertise

It all builds with what you have learned. Over time, each person develops knowledge, skills, and practical experience through work, education, relationships, and daily responsibilities. These abilities may feel ordinary to the person who possesses them, yet they often represent important ways God has been preparing them to contribute to others.
Participants begin recognizing that:

items: Skills they once considered routine may actually hold meaningful value
Strengths developed over time can become tools for serving others
God often prepares people for purpose through everyday experiences

lessonBody.text: Story

It all comes together through your story. Every person carries a unique set of life experiences that shape perspective, compassion, and understanding. As participants reflect on their story, they often begin to see how God has been present and active throughout different seasons of their life.
This reflection may reveal:

items: Experiences that shaped their perspective or strengthened their faith
Difficult seasons that now provide empathy and understanding for others
Moments where God’s guidance becomes clearer in hindsight

lessonBody.text: Desire

It all deepens with what stirs your heart. God often places interests, passions, and concerns within us that draw our attention toward particular needs or opportunities. These desires can provide important clues about where our design may naturally find expression.
Participants may begin noticing:

items: Interests or passions that consistently capture their attention
Problems or needs that move them toward action
Opportunities that feel both meaningful and energizing

lessonBody.text: Spiritual Gifts

It all strengthens when God equips you. Spiritual gifts represent the ways the Holy Spirit empowers believers to serve and build up the Body of Christ. These gifts extend beyond natural talents and reflect God’s grace working through His people.
As participants explore this area, they may begin discovering:

items: Ways God has already been working through them to encourage or strengthen others
Spiritual strengths that become evident through service and community
Opportunities to use these gifts more intentionally within the life of the church

lessonBody.text: Niche

It all leads to where your design meets God’s purpose. Niche represents the intersection where identity, expertise, story, desire, and spiritual gifts begin to align with real opportunities to serve others. Rather than defining a permanent role, niche reflects a growing awareness of how a person’s design can make a meaningful contribution.
Participants often begin asking:

items: Where do the different elements of my design naturally come together?
Who might God be inviting me to serve?
What opportunities around me could become expressions of purpose?

units.title: How to C.A.R.E
units.lessonMainIdea: Connect, Act, Reflect, and Explore.

media.label: Connect, Act, Reflect, Explore

lessonBody.text: As you move through Discover Your Divine Design, you’ll notice that this isn’t just a book to read, it’s a journey to live. To help you engage deeply with the material, we invite you to use the C.A.R.E. process, structured for the DYDD workbook. C.A.R.E. stands for Connect, Act, Reflect, and Explore, four simple but powerful approaches that will help you pause, notice, evaluate, and apply what God is showing you.

items: Connect: Engage with God, yourself, and others. Pause to notice where His hand has been shaping your story and stirring your heart (engage relationally, align with God’s movement in your life).
Act: Take the next small, faithful step. Don’t wait for perfection; move forward trusting that God meets you in motion (take faithful steps, apply insights with courage).
Reflect: Pause and notice what’s happening in and around you. Evaluate what you’re learning, where God is leading, and what’s being refined in your heart (pause, notice, and discern).
Explore: Stay curious. Ask questions, imagine new possibilities, and consider how God might be inviting you to grow beyond what you’ve seen before (stay curious, imagine, and grow).

lessonBody.text: Think of C.A.R.E. as both a compass and a rhythm: It helps you keep oriented on your journey, ensuring you’re not just gathering information but experiencing transformation. Whether you’re reading a chapter, answering workbook prompts, or journaling your thoughts, use C.A.R.E. to slow down, engage meaningfully, and allow God’s design in you to unfold with purpose.

units.title: DYDD Assessments
units.lessonMainIdea: DesignID and Spiritual Gifts support reflection, discussion, and discovery.

media.label: DesignID assessment

lessonBody.text: The DYDD Journey includes the use of two assessments, the DesignID Assessment used for identity, and the Spiritual Gifts Assessment used for understanding gifts. DesignId is a unique and custom assessment built specifically for DYDD. Both assessments will be presented as needed within the course content.

The DesignID assessment is an important part of the DYDD journey. While the class itself focuses on reflection, discussion, and discovery, DesignID provides participants with structured insight into how their design often expresses itself in real life. The assessment helps individuals recognize patterns in how they perceive situations, approach challenges, and contribute within community and ministry.

The Spiritual Gifts Assessment is designed to be a simple and reflective part of the DYDD journey. While DesignID focuses on how a person’s design tends to operate in relationships and contribution, the Spiritual Gifts Assessment helps participants consider how the Holy Spirit may be empowering them to serve within the body of Christ.

media.label: Discover your niche

lessonBody.text: The goal of the DYDD journey is not simply self-understanding. It is participation in the work God is already doing. The concept of Niche helps bring the different parts of a person’s design together so they can begin to see where their life most naturally serves others.

A niche is the place where identity, expertise, story, desire, and spiritual gifts begin to intersect. It is not a title or a position. It is the environment where a person’s design aligns with opportunities to serve and make an impact.

Many believers want to live with greater purpose but are unsure how their life fits into the larger work of God’s Kingdom. Exploring a niche helps move the conversation from general calling to practical expression. It helps people recognize where their design may be most effective and where their contribution can be most meaningful.

Understanding a niche does not mean every question about the future is answered. Instead, it provides direction. It gives individuals a clearer starting point for stepping forward in faith and exploring how God may use their life in the good works He has prepared.

As part of your journey, you will engage in active Niche building at the end of each major section. These are specifically designed CARE reflections which support your discovery process. The Pathfinder activities are an important part of completing your journey.

title: Identity

units.title: On Purpose
units.lessonMainIdea: Your identity is based on who God says you are.

media.label: Intentionally formed and shaped by God

lessonBody.text: Your Identity is so much more than your name, your job, or how others see you. Our identity is where everything begins. Throughout Scripture, we see that God shapes identity in powerful, personal ways. He calls people by name, He redefines them beyond their failures, and He reminds them that who they are is rooted in His plans, not their past. Your identity is not based on your mistakes, your achievements, or the labels others have given you. It’s based on who God says you are.
God says:

You are valuable and purposefully and wonderfully made and that was no mistake. He declares you delivered, forgiven, and healed from sin. You are redeemed, safe, and no longer separated or condemned. You are victorious and a born-again new creation. You are a child of God and member of His family who is qualified to share in His inheritance. You are part of His royal priesthood with a secure place in His kingdom. You are loved. See Psalm 139, Romans 8:1–2, Romans 8:35–37, Ephesians 1, 2 Corinthians 5:17, 1 Peter 2:9, and 1 Peter 2:24.
You were formed, pursued, made new, and shaped on purpose.

items: Formed: God’s intention was present before you could prove, perform, or produce anything. Psalm 139:13-16, Jeremiah 1:5
Pursued: Salvation is not random. God moved toward you with love, mercy, and rescue. John 3:16, Romans 5:8, Titus 3:4-5
New: In Christ, your life is not just improved. It is made new. 2 Corinthians 5:17
Shaped: God is still forming you. Your story, growth, wiring, healing, and next steps are part of His work in you. Phil 1:6, Rom 12:2, 2 Cor. 3:18

lessonBody.text: You are not accidental. You are intentionally formed, rescued, renewed, and still being shaped by God.

transcript.speaker: Mara
transcript.text: Before you try to name what you do, let God remind you whose you are. Identity is not something you perform into existence. It is received in Christ and then expressed through love. As you answer these questions, be gentle with yourself. Let truth come before pressure.

media.label: A hand resting on an open Bible

lessonBody.text: Design starts with identity. Before we explore your gifts, personality, or purpose, we need to begin with something more foundational: who you belong to.
“Who am I?” is an important question. But in discovering your divine design, it finds its deepest meaning when grounded in another question: “Whose am I?”
Who Are You?
When you describe yourself, you might talk about:

items: Your personality
Your experiences
Your talents
Your story
How others describe you

lessonBody.text: These things matter. They help you recognize what makes you unique and how you engage with the world. Your experiences have shaped your perspective. Your talents influence what comes naturally. Your personality affects how you connect, contribute, and respond.

But none of these can carry the full weight of your identity. Your abilities can change. Your roles can shift. Other people’s opinions can be mistaken. Even your own understanding of yourself can be shaped by disappointment, comparison, or past mistakes. If these become the foundation of your identity, your sense of worth can rise and fall with how well life is going.
Whose You Are?
For those who belong to Jesus, there is a deeper foundation:

items: You are a child of God.
You are fully known.
You are deeply loved.
You are secure in Christ.
You belong to the One who created you.

lessonBody.text: “Whose you are” is about belonging before achievement. You do not have to discover your gifts, prove your usefulness, or figure out your purpose to become worthy of God’s love.
See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!
Your relationship with God is not another item on the list of things that describe you. It is the foundation from which you begin to understand everything else.
Why This Matters for Your Design

When you start with “who,” discovering your design can become a search for proof that you matter. You may compare your gifts with someone else’s, wish you had a different personality, or feel that your story disqualifies you. When you start with “whose,” you can approach discovery from a place of belonging. You are not trying to earn your place in God’s family. You are learning how to live as someone who already belongs to Him.
Who you are may describe you. Whose you are defines you.

For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
Your identity in Christ is not something you earn through good works. It is the foundation from which you do them. You don’t work to become His, you serve because you already belong to Him.

God invites you into what we’re calling the Good Works Force: His people putting their God-given design into action to love others, meet needs, and make His goodness visible. This isn’t a workforce competing for recognition or earning God’s approval. It’s a people serving together, with different designs and a shared Kingdom purpose.
Your part will often take shape through:

items: Expertise — what you’ve developed
Story — what you’ve experienced
Desire — what you’re drawn toward
Gifts — what God empowers

lessonBody.text: God can work through your skills, redeem your experiences, direct your desires, and empower your gifts. Your contribution may look different from someone else’s, and that is part of the beauty of His design.

The question is not, “How do I do more?” It is, “What good is God inviting me to do with the life and design He has given me?” You don’t have to do everyone’s work. You are invited to faithfully take your part in the Good Works Force.
Purpose is not performance. It is faithful expression.

lessonBody.text: NICHE
Not doing more. Doing what fits.

Think of your God-given design as a puzzle piece. Its shape is not a flaw to correct or something to squeeze into someone else’s space. Your particular mix of skills, story, passions, and gifts shapes how you can contribute to the bigger picture of what God is doing. Your niche is where that design meets an opportunity to love, serve, and bring good to others. It is your particular contribution within the Good Works Force.

Jesus draws our attention to people who are hungry, overlooked, sick, or forgotten. Discovering your niche isn’t simply finding what makes you feel fulfilled. It is recognizing where what God has formed in you can become a meaningful gift to someone else.

That fit doesn’t mean everything will be easy or comfortable. God may stretch you as you grow into it. And you don’t need to find one perfect role before you begin. Your design can find expression in different relationships, places, and seasons.
So instead of asking, “Where can I do more?” begin asking, “Where do I see a need that connects with how God has shaped me?” You can explore that connection one faithful step at a time.
Not an identity you chase.
Not a fit you force.
A contribution you grow into

lessonBody.text: God’s design is already reflected in the way you create, relate, think, and serve. An assessment can help you recognize those patterns and give you language to explore them.

For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
A lens for identity, grace, and contribution

DesignID™ is a faith-integrated assessment that helps you explore how God’s design is expressed through your life. More than describing personality, it offers a lens for understanding how you naturally contribute within the Body of Christ.
DesignID begins with a biblical conviction: every person is made in the image of God. We each have opportunities to reflect His character through the ways we live, love, work, and serve.

Consider the DesignID wheel. At its center is God Himself—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Flowing outward are four divine reflections: Architect, Artisan, Shepherd, and Steward. These provide language for exploring different patterns of contribution.
Around the outside of the wheel are the Integrated Reflections. Each combines two reflections, helping you explore how they work together in the way you lead, build, relate, and contribute.
DesignID does not replace biblical truth, spiritual formation, or dependence on the Holy Spirit. It supports your discovery by helping you recognize your design and steward it more faithfully.

lessonBody.text: Identity doesn’t exist in isolation. God didn’t just design you for personal discovery; He designed you for connection, belonging, and purpose within the Body of Christ.

Jesus, referring to the commandment from Deuteronomy 6, tells us that we are to love God with our hearts, our souls, our minds, and our strengths. If God, who is perfect and without sin, has decided to love you, even before you repented, why do we struggle so much to love what He created? I am referring to you, of course.

One of the teachers of the law came and heard them debating. Noticing that Jesus had given them a good answer, he asked him, “Of all the commandments, which is the most important?” “The most important one,” answered Jesus, “is this: ‘Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.  Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’ The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no commandment greater than these.”

When Jesus was pointing out what the greatest two commands were, He did not say admire, like, be fond of, or adore. He said love. Every other way fails in comparison. The Greek word for love in these verses is agape. Agape means to love someone by choice as an act of your will. It is intentional and actionable. Agape is unconditional, not looking for reciprocation.
We are commanded to love, period. There is no “so that” with agape love. Often, we love so that …

items: Others change.
Someone repents.
A person or group gets saved.

lessonBody.text: First Peter 4:8 says, “Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.” We are not intended to love so that something happens, but simply to love with all our heart, mind, soul, and strength.
Heart

Your “heart” is your passions and desires. “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also” (Matthew 6:21). Loving God with your heart also means loving Him with and through your emotions. We don’t love only within fair weather but also in the tempest.
Soul

Your soul is what Jesus purchased on the cross. Our soul is of the highest value, and nothing can be measured against it. Matthew 16:26 says, “What good will it be for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for their soul?” Your soul is the eternal part of you that will go on forever. Another way to think about your soul is as your will. The good news is that God gave us free will so when we love with our soul, we are choosing to love or deciding to love with our whole being.
Mind

Your mind is your intellect, your cunning, and even your daydreaming. We use our minds to make choices or weigh decisions. It is from our minds that we reason out our need for God and choose to surrender. Your mind is a cognitive and practical approach to loving God. This does not mean that it is not highly creative and intuitive as well. It is with your mind that you build knowledge of God through study and experiences.
Strength

Loving God with your strength is letting Him have your time, your sweat, your abilities, and your possessions. When we surrender our strengths, we no longer must count on ourselves. Our strength is finite but His is infinite. Philippians 4:13 says, “I can do all this through him who gives me strength.” God’s infinite strength is available to us when we need it. “That is why, for Christ’s sake, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10).

media.label: Receiving God’s love and loving yourself

lessonBody.text: Jesus tells us to “love your neighbor as yourself,” it’s not just about being kind to others; it’s a reminder that you can’t pour out what you haven’t first received. Loving yourself isn’t selfish; it’s survival, and it’s the only way to truly love your neighbor.

Do you love yourself? Can you say it? “I love myself.” Are you able to tell others that you love yourself? If you ever want to find a way to break the ice in a conversation in a strange way, walk up to someone new next time you are out or at church and just tell them, “I really love me some me.” As funny as that sounds, based on Mark 12, you are letting them know that you are capable of loving them.
This is incredibly powerful. Loving yourself means seeing God’s perspective. How often do we put consequences, obstacles, or false perceptions above the knowledge that God loves us?

God loves you. There is no denying it. He loved you before you ever loved Him back. This includes all your blemishes, wrinkles, and scars. If you can know, truly know, that God loves you and you can surrender to being His purposeful creation, the blemishes, wrinkles, and scars, fade away. Loving yourself, the uniquely created person God designed, frees you to love others with untethered and reckless abandon. It is this type of love that will actually change your neighbors, and it is sorely missed in the fellowship of believers today.

media.label: A family together in creation

lessonBody.text: Called to “One Another”

As Christians, we are family. When we pursue harmony, mutual respect, and peace with each other, we reflect God’s character and His love. The fact that God created us all uniquely means that this unity will take work. We are called to work, love, and serve with those who are different and unfamiliar. This can create anxiety, and a multitude of miscommunications. It can lead to hurts and disagreements, or even outright conflict. All of this is not just okay but part of God’s design.

He knew that we would start our campaign as an eternal citizen in heaven, here on earth. He knew that we would grow and be refined simply because others were not like us. It is His design that we are to love in unity, being one body with many parts. Let’s face it, some of those we work with are as different as the night is from the day. Isn’t that wonderful! What an opportunity to love.

The world is watching to see if we will accept each other and love despite our differences and hang-ups, because they want to know that we will love them in the same way. What a shame it is that the Body of Christ, His bride, is so fragmented today. We have to learn to obey His commands associated with the phrase “one another.”
In the New Testament, Jesus and the apostles tell us to feel, say, or do something to one another numerous times.
Consider what it means to “one another” through your reflection. In what ways has God uniquely designed you to support and strengthen other believers?

It is important that you can “one another” for all four of your reflections. Even in the areas where you have less energy or natural capacity, the call remains the same. Every believer is invited to live out the “one another” commands of Scripture. You may simply need to lean on God’s strength more deeply in those areas, for in your weakness, He is strong.

units.title: The Journey To Expertise

media.label: A mighty oak tree

units.lessonMainIdea: The Mighty Oak, Journey

lessonBody.text: Consider the mighty oak tree. On average, an oak takes eighty to one hundred years to reach its full, mature size. That’s roughly 700,000 to 875,000 hours of standing through storms, soaking up sunlight, enduring harsh winters, and stretching toward the sky, day after day, decade after decade. Its strength doesn’t come from rushing but from a long, faithful process of becoming deeply rooted.

Your own growth is the same. Whether it’s in your faith, your gifts, your relationships, or your calling, God shapes you over time. He doesn’t expect you to become an expert overnight. Instead, He invites you to lean into a process where your natural talents grow into competence and, with practice, into mastery, not because of shortcuts, but because of deep-rooted, sustained growth.

Before we talk about what it takes to develop expertise, I want you to remember this: You are not behind. You are not late. Like the oak, you are designed for slow, faithful formation. God is shaping your expertise not for applause or achievement but for His kingdom purposes.
“Being confident of this, that he who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus” (Philippians 1:6).
A Biblical Principal
Talent: God gives the seed of talent
Competency: Faithfulness develops competency
Expertise: Time & experience cultivate expertise

units.title: Talent

media.label: A boy beginning to climb a tree

units.lessonMainIdea: Raw Ability, Inclination, Potential

lessonBody.text: Nobody wakes up one morning and is just an expert, not in learning, not in working, not in parenting, not in preaching, and definitely not in driving. (The left lane is for passing, just saying.) We all start with a spark, a talent, a curiosity, a “hey, I might be good at this” moment, and from there, it’s a winding road of practice, mistakes, growth, lots of time, and God’s grace.

We start with talent, an innate ability gifted us by God, as part of our created self. Talent is potential, ready for development through experience. It must be nurtured, refined, and developed through training, experience, and intentional practice to develop into competence, and ultimately expertise. The Bible suggests that talent is something we are instinctively born with, giving us unique skills and abilities that do not require much formal training or experience.
“For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do” Ephesians 2:10.

You may have a natural gift (innate ability) at something, but if that talent isn’t cultivated through practice, learning, or experience, it may remain at a basic level, even if that level is higher than those around you.

It is this strengthening and practice that turns talent into competency, especially as we grow in knowledge in the areas we are talented in. It makes sense, then, that as we grow in our knowledge of God, we grow in the talents He created us with. When we learn more of who He is, how He sees us, and have faith to grow in our talents, it creates competency as we become more knowledgeable about how God wants to use them.
“Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s grace in its various forms.” Peter 4:10

units.title: Competence

media.label: A young boy climbing high in a tree

units.lessonMainIdea: Reliable, Muscle Memory

lessonBody.text: Competence is that magical stage where you’ve moved past winging it but you’re not quite ready to call yourself a master. Think of it like learning to ride a bike: You’ve ditched the training wheels, you can steer without crashing into the neighbor’s mailbox, but no one’s asking you to join the Tour de France just yet. Competence is where talent starts flexing its muscles.

Some of us hesitate to call ourselves experts, and honestly, that’s okay. One of the beautiful things about God’s design is that He never demands instant mastery from us; instead, He invites us to grow, step by step. Competence is that important middle ground on the road toward expertise. It’s the phase where skills are developing, knowledge is expanding, and experience is stacking up, but you’re still in the process, not at the finish line. The real difference between competence and expertise isn’t about perfection; it’s about the depth, refinement, and maturity God helps build over time.
Competency can be defined as the crossroads of knowledge, skills, and ability.

items: Knowledge: Facts and information acquired through experience using all our senses. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; but fools despise wisdom and instruction” (Proverbs 1:7).

Skills: Specific things we develop through repetition in learned activities. “Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will serve before kings; they will not serve before officials of low rank” (Proverbs 22:29).

Ability: Performance of natural, innate skills strengthened through practice over time. “Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s grace in its various forms” (1 Peter 4:10).

lessonBody.text: Competence requires:

items: Faithfulness & intentional growth. Not cruise control.
Stewardship. Not complacency

media.label: An experienced climber using a rope

units.lessonMainIdea: Deep, Relational

lessonBody.text: Expertise used to be hard to come by. A true expert was a master of their craft who had paid the price of dedication and diligence over an extended period of time.

Nowadays, “expertise” can be found almost anywhere, and access to it is cheap and easy. Expert answers are in the palm of our hands for any topic. Knowledge has become ubiquitous, empowering the multitudes with easy access.

Expertise is more than just knowledge; it’s the application of it: wisdom. To know something only takes you so far. Experiencing it over time solidifies and hard codes it in our being as we live out the benefits or consequences. Our world is full of pseudo-experts pretending they have the answers but often cutting corners that develop glaring holes because they lack experience.
There is no shortcut to expertise. Remember the mighty oak tree.
Deep effort produces deep results.

items: Knowledge tuns into Wisdom: Info to insight
Skill becomes Intuition: Effort to instinct
Ability morphs into Credibility: Stewardship to mastery

lessonBody.text: Expertise is Devotion Formed Through Relationship

Any expert will tell you that they formed a deep and knowing relationship with the people, subject, or content in which they are considered expert. Over time, it becomes relational, personal even. The sheer volume of time and effort creates an intimacy.

The same is true about your relationship with Jesus. The more time and effort you put into your relationship with Him, the better you know Him. Consider the apostles, in particular, Peter and John. Having just spent three years of highly concentrated relationship building with Jesus, they find themselves arrested for sharing near the temple. In Acts 4 we see that they are questioned and that Peter, full of the Spirit, responded with articulate intellectual depth. Don’t forget, Peter was a fisherman, not a scholar. He was unschooled and ordinary, yet he was speaking in such a way as to astonish the most learned and academic people of the land.
“When they saw the courage of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they were astonished, and they took note that these men had been with Jesus”. Acts 4:13

Did you see it? The answer was that Peter’s expertise was relational. What astonished them about what he was courageously saying, was attributed to their time with Jesus. There having “been” with Jesus was the answer.
When it comes to expertise and faith, there are no shortcuts. The only way is the carefully slow-cooked devotion, of having been with Jesus.
Do you have knowledge of Jesus, or do you have insight?
Are you skilled at living your faith or has it become instinct?
Is your relationship with Jesus credible?

units.title: Being Vs. Doing

media.label: Two staircases in contrasting colors

units.lessonMainIdea: You are a Human Being!, Relationship before Results

lessonBody.text: We are not human doings, we are human beings!

Let’s be honest, we live in a world where “doing” gets all the applause. We make to-do lists just to cross things off and feel productive (and yes, we’ve all written something down we already did just to check it off, no judgment here). But here’s the twist. In God’s eyes, your worth isn’t measured by how many boxes you tick or how many gold stars you collect. Before you rush to do more, God invites you to be, to rest in who you are as His beloved, not just what you can accomplish. So take a deep breath, put down the checklist (it’ll still be there later), and let’s talk about why being is so important.

Psalm 46:10 says, “Be still, and know that I am God.” It is important that we learn to stop striving at times and learn to simply rest in our identity in Christ, recognizing His sovereignty and presence. The phrase “be still” in Hebrew can be defined as letting go, releasing, or stopping. In this context, it can be considered a declarative command to STOP. Psalm 46 speaks of turbulent times with war and earthquakes. This command asks us to trust that He is God and to let go of our anxieties and fears. The second part of the verse, “know that I am God,” invites us to lean not on our own understanding and accept His authority and care for all things in our lives.

At the heart of it all lies the truth of Ephesians 2:10: “For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.” This verse holds the perfect balance between being and doing. We are His handiwork—that’s our being, our identity rooted in Christ, formed by His love and redeemed by His grace. And we are created to do good works—that’s our doing, the natural outflow of who we are in Him.

Notice the order: We are before we do. The doing comes after the being, not the other way around. God doesn’t call us to create our worth through what we accomplish; He calls us to express His workmanship through what we do. Our works are not a means of earning His favor but a reflection of it. It is the living evidence that His Spirit is at work within us.

When being precedes doing, our actions become worship instead of striving. We begin to see our labor, creativity, and expertise not as self-made achievements but as divine assignments. Whether you’re teaching, leading, serving, building, healing, or creating, every good work finds meaning when it flows from your being, your relationship with Jesus.

units.careIntro: The world constantly praises productivity, yet Jesus invites us first to presence. Before you plan, perform, or pursue the next task, He calls you to sit with Him—not to earn His approval, but to remember who you already are: beloved, chosen, and enough.

units.title: Connecting Identity & Expertise

media.label: A multicultural team collaborating in a workshop

units.lessonMainIdea: Connecting Identity & Expertise

lessonBody.text: As we’ve explored, identity is the foundation of everything; it’s who you are in Christ before you lift a finger or check a single box. You are God’s beloved, redeemed, intentionally designed child. Your worth is not something you earn; it’s something you receive. It is not who you are but whose you are.

But God doesn’t stop at just being, He invites you into becoming. That’s where expertise comes in. Expertise is the tangible expression of your identity worked out over time. It’s the combination of your God-given talents, your life experiences, your practiced skills, and your growing wisdom. It’s what happens when the raw material of who you are gets shaped, refined, and multiplied to bless others.

Identity and expertise are like the roots and branches of a great oak tree. Without roots, the branches can’t stand; without branches, the roots never reach their full purpose. You were made to be deeply rooted in your identity so that what you do flows naturally from who you are. And here’s the best part: God’s not asking for instant perfection. He’s inviting you into a slow, faithful process of becoming, through trial, triumph, learning, failing, and trying again.

teachingBlocks: This Pathfinder moment turns the Niche chapter into language the learner can carry forward. The goal is not perfection; the goal is a faithful draft that captures what is becoming clear.
The mature version of this lesson should review saved reflections, surface repeated words, invite companion guidance, and preserve a draft line for the final niche declaration.

units.title: Congratulations
units.lessonMainIdea: Close the Journey with prayer, celebration, and one concrete next step beyond the course.
teachingBlocks: The ending should feel like a commissioning, not a hard stop. The learner has gathered language, evidence, prayers, and next steps that now need to be lived.
This unit can point them toward their next faithful experiment, future coaching, a Camp Circle, or deeper work with the Field Guide.
